# Write issues and pull requests through the hub

## Intent

A caller with write access to a workspace creates and changes the issues, comments, labels and pull requests of that workspace's forge repository through the hub, with the credential the hub stores for the workspace, so that no agent ever holds a forge token. The hub never writes to a forge without a stored credential, refuses a bad request before anything is sent, and leaves exactly one hub event for every write that reached the forge, whether it succeeded or failed.

## Goals

- Nine write routes under `/api/v1/workspaces/:slug` work on GitHub and on GitLab: create issue, update issue, close issue, comment on an issue, add labels, remove a label, ensure a label, open a pull request, comment on a pull request.
- Every write route needs the scope `forge:write` and write access, is refused with `409 workspace_archived` on an archived workspace and with `422 forge_credential_missing` when the workspace has no stored credential for the target; a refused request sends nothing to the forge and records no event.
- Text is measured before anything is sent: more than 65,536 characters on GitHub or 1,000,000 on GitLab is `413 payload_too_large`.
- A write that sent at least one request to the forge records exactly one `parley.forge.*` event before its response, with `ok` true or false, and never a title, a body, a comment text, a credential or a forge error message.
- The five `POST` routes that create something can be retried with an `Idempotency-Key`: the replay sends nothing to the forge and records no event.
- A write runs to its end and records its event when the caller disconnects.
- Nine CLI commands call the routes: `parley issue create|update|close|comment|label|unlabel`, `parley label create`, `parley pr create|comment`.

## Non-goals

- Forge detection, the remote target, the forge client and its outbound rules (user agent, proxy, redirects, the 30-second deadline, the 8 MiB read limit, the rate-limit retry), the `:number` rule, the resolution of a task fork to its parent's forge, the error mapping and the scrubbing of forge messages (FRG-FR-001 to FRG-FR-013, FRG-FR-029 to FRG-FR-031), the read routes and the read commands of `parley forge|issue|pr`: package 41 `forge_reads`. This package states what a caller of a write route observes of those rules and builds on that package's code.
- The webhook secret routes `PUT` and `DELETE …/forge/webhook`, their events `parley.forge.webhook.set` and `.unset`, the ingress `/hooks/forge/:slug`, the delivery log and `parley forge webhook|deliveries` (FRG-FR-032 to FRG-FR-041): package 43 `forge_webhook_ingress`.
- The error envelope, the order of the platform's checks, the rules of `Idempotency-Key` and the body size and content type rules (PLAT-FR-010 to PLAT-FR-019): package 02 `http_api_conventions`.
- The CLI's settings, HTTP client, output and exit codes (PLAT-FR-090 to PLAT-FR-095): package 09 `cli_foundation`.
- The event record, its common fields, visibility and the event stream: package 52 `durable_event_log_and_stream`.
- The workspace settings `forge_api_url` and `upstream_forge_api_url`: package 11 `workspace_read_update_settings`. The git credentials of a workspace: packages 10 `workspace_create_and_clone` and 39 `secrets`; the upstream credential for the forge is resolved by package 41 with the secret names and the order of package 31 `carry_patch_setup_and_patches`.
- Pushing a branch to origin so that a pull request can name it: package 13 `workspace_push_to_origin`.
- Updating, merging or closing a pull request, deleting a comment or a label, resolving GitLab assignee names to user ids: the source PRD has no such route (§12.5).
- Any link between a forge object and a change: the two are independent (§12.1).

## Background

The repository holds no code yet; every file named here is new, except the files other packages create and this one extends: `internal/cli/issue.go` and `internal/cli/pr.go`, which package 41 creates for its read commands.

Package 41 delivers, in `internal/forge/`: the resolution of a route's workspace, target and forge configuration (repository, forge kind, API URL, credential kind, and for a task fork the parent); the forge client with its outbound rules; the result types issue, comment and pull request and their mapping from GitHub and GitLab answers (package 41 has no label type; this package adds one, see Design Decision 7); the fake forge `internal/forge/forgetest/`, which this package extends with the write endpoints; the mapping of a failed forge call to a status and an `error_type`; and the scrubbing of forge messages. This package adds the write routes on top of them, in new files of `internal/forge/`, and the write commands in `internal/cli/`. Where this document says "package 41's …", the coder uses whatever name that package gave the part and does not write a second one.

Hub events are recorded through the event component of package 52 in `internal/event/`. `Idempotency-Key` is handled by the create-route helper of package 02 in `internal/server/`. The CLI commands are declared with the command helper of package 09 in `internal/cli/`.

## Requirements

### Access and order of checks on a write route (FRG-FR-001, FRG-FR-002, FRG-FR-004, FRG-FR-007, FRG-FR-025, §12.10)

The nine write routes are:

| Route | Does | Success | Event |
|---|---|---|---|
| `POST /workspaces/:slug/issues` | create issue | `201`, the issue | `parley.forge.issue.create` |
| `PATCH /workspaces/:slug/issues/:number` | update issue | `200`, the issue | `parley.forge.issue.update` |
| `POST /workspaces/:slug/issues/:number/close` | close issue | `200`, the issue | `parley.forge.issue.close` |
| `POST /workspaces/:slug/issues/:number/comments` | comment on an issue | `201`, `{"url"}` | `parley.forge.comment.create` |
| `POST /workspaces/:slug/issues/:number/labels` | add labels | `204` | `parley.forge.label.add` |
| `DELETE /workspaces/:slug/issues/:number/labels/:name` | remove a label | `204` | `parley.forge.label.remove` |
| `POST /workspaces/:slug/labels` | ensure a label | `200` or `201`, the label | `parley.forge.label.create` |
| `POST /workspaces/:slug/pulls` | open a pull request | `201`, the pull request | `parley.forge.pull_request.create` |
| `POST /workspaces/:slug/pulls/:number/comments` | comment on a pull request | `201`, `{"url"}` | `parley.forge.pull_request.comment` |

Every write route needs the scope `forge:write` and write access to the workspace, and takes the query parameter `target`. A PAT without the scope gets `403 insufficient_scope`, also for a slug that does not exist. A caller with read access only (a read-only org member) gets `403 forbidden`, also on an archived workspace, because access comes before state. A caller with no access gets `404 not_found`.

After the platform's checks, a write route checks in this order, and the first failure decides the answer (FRG-FR-002):

1. `target`: given twice or with a value other than `origin` and `upstream` → `400 invalid_request`; `upstream` on a workspace that is not a carry-patch workspace with an `upstream_url` → `400 workspace_mode_mismatch`.
2. The path parameters and the body, as far as they do not depend on the forge kind → `400 invalid_request`. A bad `:number` has the message `number must be a positive decimal integer`.
3. The workspace is archived → `409 workspace_archived`; the route was called through a task fork whose parent is archived → `409 parent_archived`.
4. Forge configuration → `422 forge_api_url_invalid` or `422 forge_unknown`.
5. Checks that depend on the forge kind: GitLab assignees (FRG-FR-017) → `400`; text limits (FRG-FR-024) → `413`.
6. The credential kind for the target is `none` → `422 forge_credential_missing` (FRG-FR-025).
7. The call.

A request refused before step 7 sends nothing to the forge, including the lookups some writes begin with, and records no event. Two consequences the source PRD names: malformed JSON is `400` even when the forge cannot be detected, and an oversized text on a workspace with an unknown forge is `422`, because the limit depends on the forge kind.

No write route needs the hub's copy of the repository, and none answers `workspace_busy`.

**Task forks.** A write route called with a fork's slug acts on the parent's forge repository with the parent's credential and the parent's settings, including `target=upstream`. The caller must have write access on the parent; without it the answer is `403 forbidden`. A token bound to the fork is accepted; the access that counts is that of the user behind it.

**Upstream.** With `target=upstream` on a carry-patch workspace that has an `upstream_url`, the write goes to the upstream repository, through the API URL of `upstream_forge_api_url` or the default of the upstream host, with the upstream git credential, which falls back to the origin credential.

### Bodies and text limits (FRG-FR-014, FRG-FR-024)

A write body is a JSON object, except on the add-labels route, where it is a bare JSON array, and on the close route, where it may also be empty. An absent field and a `null` field both mean "not set". Unknown fields are ignored. A required string must not be blank. A list of names has at most 100 entries, none blank. A violation is `400 invalid_request`, and the message names the field.

Long text is refused before anything is sent: more than 65,536 characters on GitHub, more than 1,000,000 on GitLab, counted in Unicode code points. The measured fields are the `body` of an issue (create and update), of a comment and of a pull request, and the `comment` of a close. Over the limit → `413 payload_too_large`, with a message that names the field, its length and the limit. A text of exactly the limit is accepted.

### Create and update an issue (FRG-FR-015 to FRG-FR-017)

**Create.** Body `{"title": string, "body"?: string, "labels"?: [string], "assignees"?: [string]}`. `title` is required. Answers `201` with the issue.

**Update.** Body with any of `title` (not blank), `body` (`""` clears it), `state` (`open` or `closed`), `labels` and `assignees` (each replaces the whole set; `[]` clears it). Only the fields that are set are sent. No field set → `400 invalid_request`. Answers `200` with the issue as the forge returns it.

**GitLab assignees.** GitLab takes assignees as user ids, which the hub does not resolve. On GitLab `assignees` is not sent on create or update; the other fields are. An update whose only set field is `assignees` is refused with `400 invalid_request`; nothing is sent.

### Close an issue (FRG-FR-018)

The body may be empty or `{"comment": string}`. A non-blank comment is posted first; the issue is closed only if the comment succeeded. If the comment fails, the answer is that failure and the issue is untouched. If the close fails after the comment was posted, the answer is the close's failure and the event carries `comment_url`. Closing a closed issue succeeds. Answers `200` with the issue.

### Comment on an issue or a pull request (FRG-FR-019)

Body `{"body": string}`, required. Answers `201` with `{"url": "<web URL of the comment>"}`. On the pull-request route the comment goes to the pull request's conversation.

### Labels (FRG-FR-020 to FRG-FR-022)

**Add labels.** The body is a bare JSON array of 1 to 100 non-blank names. The labels are added and the issue keeps its others. Answers `204`.

**Remove a label.** The label is the last path segment, percent-decoded once, so `type%2Fbug` names `type/bug`. A blank or undecodable name is `400`. The route is idempotent: `204` when the issue exists, whether or not it carried the label; `404 forge_not_found` when the issue does not exist.

**Ensure a label.** Body `{"name": string, "color"?: string, "description"?: string}`. `name` is required; `color` is six hex digits with or without a leading `#`, default `ededed`. If the repository has a label of that name, the answer is `200` with the label as the forge holds it, unchanged. Otherwise the label is created and the answer is `201`. If two callers race, the loser answers `200` with the winner's label.

### Open a pull request (FRG-FR-023)

Body `{"title": string, "head": string, "base": string, "body"?: string, "draft"?: boolean}`. `title`, `head` and `base` are required; `draft` defaults to `false`. `head` is sent as given, so `owner:branch` names a branch of a forge-side fork. Both branches must exist on the forge. A pull request that already exists for the same head and base is the forge's refusal (`422 forge_rejected`). Answers `201` with the pull request.

### Forge failures, disconnects and replays (FRG-FR-026, FRG-FR-027, FRG-FR-029 to FRG-FR-031)

A forge call of a write that fails is answered with the mapping of package 41: `404 forge_not_found`, `422 forge_rejected`, `429 forge_rate_limited` (with `Retry-After` when the forge stated a wait), `502 forge_unauthenticated`, `502 forge_forbidden`, `502 forge_error`, `502 forge_unreachable`, `504 forge_timeout`. The message is scrubbed and carries no credential.

A write is not abandoned when the caller disconnects. It runs to its end and its event is recorded.

The five `POST` routes that create something (issue, issue comment, pull-request comment, label, pull request) accept `Idempotency-Key` as §3 specifies: a replay answers `200` with the original body, sends nothing to the forge and records no event.

### Events (FRG-FR-028, §12.8)

A write route records exactly one `parley.forge.*` event when it sent at least one request to the forge, whether the write succeeded or failed. The event is recorded before the response is sent.

The actor is the caller. `workspace` is the workspace whose forge was written; for a call through a task fork that is the parent, and `metadata.fork` holds the fork's slug. Common metadata: `target`, `ok`, `error_type` (when `ok` is false), `number` (when known) and `url` (the web URL of the resulting issue, pull request or comment, when known).

| Event | `resource_type` | `resource_id` | `action` | Extra metadata |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `parley.forge.issue.create` | `issue` | the new number; `none` on failure | `create` | none |
| `parley.forge.issue.update` | `issue` | number | `update` | `fields` (names of the fields sent, sorted) |
| `parley.forge.issue.close` | `issue` | number | `close` | `comment_url` (when a comment was posted) |
| `parley.forge.comment.create` | `comment` | issue number | `create` | none |
| `parley.forge.label.add` | `label` | issue number | `add` | `labels` |
| `parley.forge.label.remove` | `label` | issue number | `remove` | `label` |
| `parley.forge.label.create` | `label` | label name | `create` | `label`, `created` (true only when this call created it) |
| `parley.forge.pull_request.create` | `pull_request` | the new number; `none` on failure | `create` | `head`, `base`, `draft` |
| `parley.forge.pull_request.comment` | `pull_request` | number | `comment` | none |

No forge event ever carries a title of a write, a body, a comment text, a credential or a forge error message.

### CLI (§12.6)

The conventions of §3 apply. Every command prints the hub's answer unless a different output is stated. Slugs, numbers and label names are sent as single percent-encoded path segments. A flag that is not given sends nothing. `<number>` is checked with the rule of FRG-FR-006 before anything is sent; a violation is a usage error (exit 2). Every command takes `--target <origin|upstream>`. Text input: `--body <text>` gives the text; `--body-file <path>` reads it from a file, or from stdin when the path is `-`. The text is sent exactly as given. Giving both is a usage error.

| Command | Route | Flags and output |
|---|---|---|
| `parley issue create <workspace-slug>` | `POST …/issues` | `--title` (required), `--body` or `--body-file`, `--label` (repeatable, one name each), `--assignee` (repeatable) |
| `parley issue update <workspace-slug> <number>` | `PATCH …/issues/:number` | `--title`, `--body` or `--body-file`, `--state`, `--label` (repeatable), `--assignee` (repeatable); only the given fields are sent; no field flag is a usage error; `--body ""` clears the body |
| `parley issue close <workspace-slug> <number>` | `POST …/issues/:number/close` | `--comment <text>` |
| `parley issue comment <workspace-slug> <number>` | `POST …/issues/:number/comments` | `--body` or `--body-file` (one is required) |
| `parley issue label <workspace-slug> <number> <label>...` | `POST …/issues/:number/labels` | prints `{"status":"labeled","number":<n>,"labels":[…]}` |
| `parley issue unlabel <workspace-slug> <number> <label>` | `DELETE …/issues/:number/labels/:name` | prints `{"status":"unlabeled","number":<n>,"label":"<label>"}` |
| `parley label create <workspace-slug> <name>` | `POST …/labels` | `--color <hex>`, `--description <text>`; exit 0 whether the label existed or was created |
| `parley pr create <workspace-slug>` | `POST …/pulls` | `--title`, `--head`, `--base` (all required), `--body` or `--body-file`, `--draft` |
| `parley pr comment <workspace-slug> <number>` | `POST …/pulls/:number/comments` | `--body` or `--body-file` (one is required) |

### End-to-end flows

- An agent runs `parley issue create demo --title … --label bug`, then `parley issue label demo 7 triage` and `parley issue comment demo 7 --body …`. The parley CLI sends each request; `parleyd` checks scope, access, the body, the workspace state, the forge configuration, the text limit and the credential, calls the forge with the workspace's stored token, records one event per write and answers. The forge holds the issue, both labels and the comment; the event log holds three events with `ok` true; no answer and no event contains the token.
- An agent sends `POST /workspaces/demo/pulls` with an `Idempotency-Key`, loses the answer and sends the same request again. `parleyd` opens the pull request on the forge once, records one `parley.forge.pull_request.create` event, and answers the second request `200` with the first answer without contacting the forge.

## Design Decisions

1. **Language and tests (project-wide).** Go; HTTP uses `net/http` and its method-and-pattern router; the CLI uses `github.com/spf13/cobra`; tests are table-driven with `testing` and `net/http/httptest`. A test forge is an `httptest` TLS server that plays GitHub or GitLab; the handlers are built with the forge client's transport as a parameter so that tests trust it. In tests the forge kind comes from the remote's host (`github.com`, `gitlab.com`) or from a `forge_api_url` whose path contains `github` or `gitlab` (the kind rule of §12.3 looks at the whole URL).
2. **Webhook routes are not in this package.** FRG-FR-001 and FRG-FR-004 call the webhook `PUT` a write, but the plan gives webhook secret management to package 43. "Write route" here means the nine routes above. Package 43 applies the same preconditions to its `PUT`, in the same order where both have them: scope `forge:write`, write access (`403 forbidden` for read access only, also on an archived workspace), the body, then `409 workspace_archived`. Its routes take no `target` and refuse a task fork with `400 fork_has_no_origin` instead of acting on the parent, so they never answer `parent_archived`; they call no forge, so the forge configuration and credential steps do not apply; `503 secrets_unavailable` and `429 secret_limit_reached` are theirs alone, because no route of this package stores a secret.
3. **Blank** means empty or made of Unicode white space only. The source PRD does not define it.
4. **What the hub sends** (unverified; taken from the forges' public REST APIs, to be confirmed by the coder against the forges' documentation). Paths are relative to the API URL; `R` is `/repos/<owner>/<name>` on GitHub and `/projects/<owner/name as one percent-encoded segment>` on GitLab; label names in a path are one percent-encoded segment.

   | Write | GitHub | GitLab |
   |---|---|---|
   | create issue | `POST R/issues` `{title, body, labels, assignees}` | `POST R/issues` `{title, description, labels}` |
   | update issue | `PATCH R/issues/<n>` `{title, body, state, labels, assignees}` | `PUT R/issues/<n>` `{title, description, state_event, labels}`; `state` `closed` is `state_event` `close`, `open` is `reopen` |
   | close issue | `PATCH R/issues/<n>` `{state: "closed"}` | `PUT R/issues/<n>` `{state_event: "close"}` |
   | comment on an issue | `POST R/issues/<n>/comments` `{body}` | `POST R/issues/<n>/notes` `{body}` |
   | comment on a pull request | `POST R/issues/<n>/comments` `{body}` | `POST R/merge_requests/<n>/notes` `{body}` |
   | add labels | `POST R/issues/<n>/labels` `{labels}` | `PUT R/issues/<n>` `{add_labels}` |
   | remove a label | `DELETE R/issues/<n>/labels/<name>`; on `404`, `GET R/issues/<n>` | `PUT R/issues/<n>` `{remove_labels}` |
   | ensure a label | `GET R/labels/<name>`, then `POST R/labels` `{name, color, description}` | `GET R/labels/<name>`, then `POST R/labels` `{name, color: "#<hex>", description}` |
   | open a pull request | `POST R/pulls` `{title, head, base, body, draft}` | `POST R/merge_requests` `{title, source_branch, target_branch, description}` |

   A field that is not set is left out of the forge request. On GitLab a list of label names is sent as one comma-separated string, as its API takes it; the hub does not refuse a name that contains a comma.
5. **Remove a label on GitHub.** GitHub answers `404` both when the issue is missing and when the issue does not carry the label. On a `404` the hub reads the issue: if it exists the answer is `204`, otherwise `404 forge_not_found`. Any other failure of either call is mapped as usual.
6. **Ensure a label.** The hub looks the label up by name first. A `404` of the lookup means "no such label" and leads to the create; any other lookup failure is the answer. When the create is refused because the label now exists (GitHub `422`, GitLab `409`), the hub looks the label up once more and answers `200` with it; if that lookup does not find it, the answer is the create's mapped refusal. An existing label is never changed, also when the request's `color` or `description` differ.
7. **Colour form.** `color` is accepted in either letter case and sent in lower case, without `#` to GitHub and with `#` to GitLab. Package 41 reads no labels as objects, so this package adds the label type `{name, color, description}` to `internal/forge/types.go` with its GitHub and GitLab mappings; `color` in an answer is six lower-case hex digits without `#`, and an absent description is `""`.
8. **A draft on GitLab** is a merge request whose title begins with `Draft: `; the hub adds that prefix when `draft` is true and the title does not already begin with it. `head` is sent as `source_branch` as given; the hub does not resolve `owner:branch` to a GitLab project.
9. **The comment's web URL** comes from package 41's comment mapping, the one its comments list uses, so that a comment has one URL whether it is read or written.
10. **`fields` of the update event** names the fields sent to the forge, sorted. On GitLab `assignees` is never among them.
11. **Which `POST` routes take `Idempotency-Key`.** The five that create something. The close route and the add-labels route create no resource; the header is ignored there and each request is carried out.
12. **A request counts as sent** from the moment the hub hands it to the forge client, also when the connection fails or the deadline passes. Such a write records its event with `ok` false.
13. **The write survives a disconnect** because the forge calls and the event write do not use the request's cancellation; each forge request keeps its own 30-second deadline.
14. **An event that cannot be recorded** makes the answer `500 internal`. What the forge did is not undone. The source PRD does not say; a success without its event would break "exactly one event". Events are recorded with the event component of package 52 (`EmitNow`, since a forge write has no store transaction of its own). Package 43 answers `500 internal` in the same case on its management routes, where the secret change and the event share one transaction and are both rolled back.
15. **`url` and `number` in the event.** `number` is the issue or pull-request number of the path, or the new number after a create; it is absent on `parley.forge.label.create` and on a failed create. `url` is the web URL of the issue (create, update, close), of the pull request (create) or of the comment (the two comment routes); it is absent on the three label events and on a failure that produced no object.
16. **The close body.** Empty, `{}`, `{"comment": null}` and a blank `comment` all close without a comment. A `comment` that is not a string is `400 invalid_request`.
17. **An undecodable label segment** (`%zz`) never reaches the handler: the HTTP layer of package 02 answers `400` for a request target that cannot be parsed. `%252F` decodes once, to the name `%2F`.
18. **CLI details the source PRD leaves open.** A missing required flag, both `--body` and `--body-file`, a `--body-file` that cannot be read and `issue update` without a field flag are `usage_error` (exit 2), raised before any request. `parley issue close` sends no body without `--comment` and `{"comment": <text>}` with it. `--state` is sent as given; the hub validates it. `--draft` not given sends no `draft` member. `--target` and the `<number>` check are the helpers of package 41's read commands. The CLI sends no `Idempotency-Key`.
19. **Nothing is stored per workspace** by this package, so it registers nothing with the workspace deletion registry of package 14.

## Glossary

- **Hub**: The `parleyd` server.
- **Workspace**: A repository the hub holds, identified by its `slug`. Either a registered repository or a task fork.
- **Origin**: A registered workspace's remote (`git_url`).
- **Task fork (fork)**: A workspace created from another workspace (its parent) for one task. It shares history with the parent, has its own branches and expires: after 7 days by default, or 24 hours after all its changes have landed or been abandoned.
- **Carry-patch workspace**: A workspace that tracks an upstream project and keeps an ordered list of patches on top of it.
- **Upstream**: For a carry-patch workspace, the project it tracks (`upstream_url`).
- **Scope / permission**: A string carried by a PAT that grants read or write access to an area.
- **Bound token**: A PAT confined to one workspace (and the forks created with it). A token bound to a fork also reaches its own changes, and the awareness and policy reads, on the fork's parent (§3).
- **Hub event**: A record of something the hub did (`parley.*` types), with a sequence number. Hub events form the audit log and the event stream.
- **Forge**: GitHub or GitLab, where a workspace's repository lives.
- **Forge kind**: `github` or `gitlab`, decided from the API URL setting or the remote's host (§12.3).
- **Remote target**: The repository a forge route works on, chosen by the query parameter `target`: `origin` (the default) or `upstream`.
- **Credential kind**: What the hub sends to the forge for a target: `pat` (the stored token), `basic` (the stored password, as the token) or `none`.
- **Write route**: One of the nine routes of this package that change something on the forge.
- **Pull request**: A forge pull request; on GitLab a merge request, numbered by its project-level `iid`.

# Requirements

## Requirements

### REQ-1: Access and order of checks on a write route

**Rationale:** A caller must get the same refusal, for the same reason, on every write route, and a refused write must leave no trace on the forge or in the event log.

#### Criteria

1. [REQ-1.1] IF a write route is called with a PAT that lacks the scope `forge:write`, or by a caller whose access to the workspace is below write, THEN THE parleyd SHALL refuse the request before it reads the body or the workspace state
   → HTTP 403 with `error_type` `insufficient_scope` for a PAT without `forge:write`, also when the slug names no workspace; HTTP 403 with `error_type` `forbidden` for a caller with read access only, also when the workspace is archived; HTTP 404 with `error_type` `not_found` for a caller with no access; the forge receives no request and no event is recorded
   Check: unit
   - setup: a GitHub workspace `demo` (remote `https://github.com/acme/widgets.git`, credential kind `pat`, `forge_api_url` pointing at the test forge) with the caller as its owner
   - setup: an org workspace that a second user can read but not write, and an archived copy of it
   - setup: a test forge (`httptest` TLS server) that records every request it receives and answers as GitHub or GitLab would
   - setup: an event recorder in place of the event log
   - setup: the write routes {POST issues, PATCH issues/7, POST issues/7/close, POST issues/7/comments, POST issues/7/labels, DELETE issues/7/labels/bug, POST labels, POST pulls, POST pulls/7/comments}, each with a valid body
   ```
   in internal/forge/write_test.go, a table over every write route x the callers {PAT with `forge:read` only on `demo`, the same PAT on the unknown slug `nope`, a read-only org member on `demo`, the same member on an archived workspace, a user with no access}: r = call(route, caller); assert (r.status, r.json.error.error_type) == (403, 'insufficient_scope') for the two PAT rows, (403, 'forbidden') for the two member rows, (404, 'not_found') for the last; assert forge.requests == 0 and events.count == 0
   ```
1. [REQ-1.2] IF a write route is called by a caller with write access on a workspace whose status is `archived`, THEN THE parleyd SHALL refuse the request
   → HTTP 409 with `error_type` `workspace_archived`; the forge receives no request and no event is recorded
   Check: unit
   - setup: an archived GitHub workspace `old` with credential kind `pat` and the caller as its owner
   - setup: a test forge (`httptest` TLS server) that records every request it receives and answers as GitHub or GitLab would
   - setup: an event recorder in place of the event log
   - setup: the write routes {POST issues, PATCH issues/7, POST issues/7/close, POST issues/7/comments, POST issues/7/labels, DELETE issues/7/labels/bug, POST labels, POST pulls, POST pulls/7/comments}, each with a valid body
   ```
   in internal/forge/write_test.go, a table over every write route: r = call(route, owner, slug='old'); assert r.status == 409 and r.json.error.error_type == 'workspace_archived'; assert forge.requests == 0 and events.count == 0
   ```
1. [REQ-1.3] WHEN a write route is called with the slug of a task fork by a caller who has write access on the fork's parent, THE parleyd SHALL carry out the write on the parent's forge repository, with the parent's stored credential and the parent's forge settings, including `target=upstream` when the parent is a carry-patch workspace with an `upstream_url`
   → the answer is the one the same request gives on the parent's slug; the forge request names the parent's repository and carries the parent's token
   Check: unit
   - setup: a GitHub workspace `demo` (remote `https://github.com/acme/widgets.git`, credential kind `pat`, `forge_api_url` pointing at the test forge) with the caller as its owner
   - setup: a task fork `demo-fork` of `demo` owned by the caller, with no credential and no forge settings of its own
   - setup: a test forge (`httptest` TLS server) that records every request it receives and answers as GitHub or GitLab would
   - setup: an event recorder in place of the event log
   ```
   in internal/forge/write_test.go: r = post('/workspaces/demo-fork/issues', {title:'t'}); assert r.status == 201; assert forge.last.path == '/repos/acme/widgets/issues' and forge.last.header('Authorization') carries the token of `demo`; repeat with a fork-bound PAT of the same user and assert 201
   ```
1. [REQ-1.4] IF a write route is called with the slug of a task fork and the caller has less than write access on the fork's parent, or the parent's status is `archived`, THEN THE parleyd SHALL refuse the request
   → HTTP 403 with `error_type` `forbidden` when the caller lacks write access on the parent; HTTP 409 with `error_type` `parent_archived` when the parent is archived and the caller has write access on it; the forge receives no request and no event is recorded
   Check: unit
   - setup: an org workspace with a task fork owned by a member whose access to the parent is read only
   - setup: an archived workspace with a task fork owned by the parent's owner
   - setup: a test forge (`httptest` TLS server) that records every request it receives and answers as GitHub or GitLab would
   - setup: an event recorder in place of the event log
   ```
   in internal/forge/write_test.go, a table over {fork owned by an org member who can only read the parent -> (403, 'forbidden'); fork of an archived parent, caller owns both -> (409, 'parent_archived'); fork of an archived parent, caller can only read the parent -> (403, 'forbidden')}: r = post('/workspaces/<fork>/issues', {title:'t'}); assert status and error_type; assert forge.requests == 0 and events.count == 0
   ```
1. [REQ-1.5] IF a write route passes every earlier check and the credential kind for the target is `none`, THEN THE parleyd SHALL refuse the request without sending anything to the forge, including the lookup a label removal or a label ensure would begin with
   → HTTP 422 with `error_type` `forge_credential_missing`; the forge receives no request and no event is recorded
   Check: unit
   - setup: a GitHub workspace `anon` with no stored git credential and the caller as its owner
   - setup: a GitHub workspace `basic` whose stored credential is a username and a password
   - setup: a test forge (`httptest` TLS server) that records every request it receives and answers as GitHub or GitLab would
   - setup: an event recorder in place of the event log
   - setup: the write routes {POST issues, PATCH issues/7, POST issues/7/close, POST issues/7/comments, POST issues/7/labels, DELETE issues/7/labels/bug, POST labels, POST pulls, POST pulls/7/comments}, each with a valid body
   ```
   in internal/forge/write_test.go, a table over every write route: r = call(route, owner, slug='anon'); assert r.status == 422 and r.json.error.error_type == 'forge_credential_missing'; assert forge.requests == 0 and events.count == 0; then the same table with a workspace whose credential kind is `basic`: assert the forge request carries the stored password as the token
   ```
1. [REQ-1.6] THE parleyd SHALL for any write request that fails more than one check, answer with the failure that comes first in this order: `target`; path parameters and body rules that do not depend on the forge kind; archived workspace or archived parent; forge configuration; GitLab assignees rule and text limits; missing credential
   → one error envelope whose status and `error_type` are those of the first failing check; the forge receives no request and no event is recorded
   Check: unit
   - setup: workspaces owned by the caller for each row: archived, unknown forge (remote host `code.example.com`, no `forge_api_url`), a stored `forge_api_url` that is not a valid URL, GitHub without credential, GitLab without credential
   - setup: a test forge (`httptest` TLS server) that records every request it receives and answers as GitHub or GitLab would
   - setup: an event recorder in place of the event log
   ```
   in internal/forge/write_test.go, a table of requests that each fail two checks, with the expected first: {target=bogus + malformed JSON -> (400, 'invalid_request') naming target; target=upstream on a non-carry-patch workspace + number '07' -> (400, 'workspace_mode_mismatch'); number '0' on an archived workspace -> (400, 'invalid_request') with message 'number must be a positive decimal integer'; malformed JSON on a workspace with an unknown forge -> (400, 'invalid_request'); blank title on an archived workspace -> (400, 'invalid_request'); archived workspace with an unknown forge -> (409, 'workspace_archived'); body of 65,537 characters on a workspace with an unknown forge -> (422, 'forge_unknown'); invalid `forge_api_url` + no credential -> (422, 'forge_api_url_invalid'); GitLab update with only `assignees` + no credential -> (400, 'invalid_request'); GitHub body of 65,537 characters + no credential -> (413, 'payload_too_large'); target given twice -> (400, 'invalid_request')}: assert status and error_type per row; assert forge.requests == 0 and events.count == 0
   ```
1. [REQ-1.7] WHEN a write route is called with `target=upstream` on a carry-patch workspace that has an `upstream_url`, THE parleyd SHALL carry out the write on the upstream repository, through the API URL of `upstream_forge_api_url` or the default of the upstream host, with the upstream git credential or, when none is stored, the origin credential
   → the forge request names the upstream repository and carries the upstream token; the recorded event has metadata `target` `upstream`; without `target`, or with `target=origin`, the request names the origin repository and the event has `target` `origin`
   Check: unit
   - setup: a carry-patch GitHub workspace `cp` with origin `acme/widgets`, upstream `upstream/project`, both API URL settings pointing at the test forge and the caller as its owner
   - setup: a test forge (`httptest` TLS server) that records every request it receives and answers as GitHub or GitLab would
   - setup: an event recorder in place of the event log
   ```
   in internal/forge/write_test.go, a table over {target absent, target=origin, target=upstream with an upstream credential, target=upstream with only the origin credential}: r = post('/workspaces/cp/issues' + query, {title:'t'}); assert r.status == 201; assert forge.last.path names `acme/widgets` for the origin rows and `upstream/project` for the upstream rows; assert the token sent is the upstream one, or the origin one in the last row; assert events.last.metadata.target equals the target of the row
   ```

### REQ-2: Write bodies and text limits

**Rationale:** A body the forge would reject or truncate is refused by the hub with a message that names the field, before any request leaves.

#### Criteria

1. [REQ-2.1] IF the body of a write route is not valid JSON, is not a JSON object on a route that takes an object, or is not a JSON array on the add-labels route, THEN THE parleyd SHALL refuse the request
   → HTTP 400 with `error_type` `invalid_request`; the forge receives no request and no event is recorded
   Check: unit
   - setup: a GitHub workspace `demo` (remote `https://github.com/acme/widgets.git`, credential kind `pat`, `forge_api_url` pointing at the test forge) with the caller as its owner
   - setup: a test forge (`httptest` TLS server) that records every request it receives and answers as GitHub or GitLab would
   - setup: an event recorder in place of the event log
   ```
   in internal/forge/write_test.go, a table over the routes that require a body {POST issues, PATCH issues/7, POST issues/7/comments, POST labels, POST pulls, POST pulls/7/comments} x the bodies {`{` (malformed), `[]`, `"x"`, `5`, none}, plus POST issues/7/labels x {`{`, `{}`, `"bug"`, none} and POST issues/7/close x {`{`, `[]`, `5`}: assert r.status == 400 and r.json.error.error_type == 'invalid_request'; assert forge.requests == 0 and events.count == 0
   ```
1. [REQ-2.2] IF a field of a write body breaks its rule: a required string is absent, null or blank; a field has the wrong JSON type; a list of names has more than 100 entries, a blank entry or an entry that is not a string; the add-labels array is empty; `state` is neither `open` nor `closed`; `color` is not six hex digits with or without a leading `#`, THEN THE parleyd SHALL refuse the request and name the offending field in the message
   → HTTP 400 with `error_type` `invalid_request` and a `message` that contains the field's name; the forge receives no request and no event is recorded
   Check: unit
   - setup: a GitHub workspace `demo` (remote `https://github.com/acme/widgets.git`, credential kind `pat`, `forge_api_url` pointing at the test forge) with the caller as its owner
   - setup: a test forge (`httptest` TLS server) that records every request it receives and answers as GitHub or GitLab would
   - setup: an event recorder in place of the event log
   ```
   in internal/forge/write_test.go, a table of (route, body, field): {POST issues: no title, title null, title '  ', title 5, labels 'bug', labels of 101 names, labels ['a',''], labels ['a',5], assignees of 101 names, body 5}; {PATCH issues/7: title '', title ' \t', state 'merged', state 5, labels [' ']}; {POST issues/7/close: comment 5}; {POST issues/7/comments and POST pulls/7/comments: no body, body '', body ' ', body null}; {POST issues/7/labels: [], 101 names, ['a',' '], ['a',5]}; {POST labels: no name, name ' ', color 'red', color '#12345', color 'ededed0', color 5, description 5}; {POST pulls: no title, no head, no base, head ' ', draft 'yes'}: assert r.status == 400 and r.json.error.error_type == 'invalid_request' and r.json.error.message contains field; assert forge.requests == 0 and events.count == 0. Boundary rows that must pass validation: labels of exactly 100 names, a 100-name add-labels array, color '#EDEDED', color 'abcdef'
   ```
1. [REQ-2.3] THE parleyd SHALL for any write body, treat a member whose value is `null` exactly as an absent member and ignore members it does not know
   → the forge request and the answer are the same as for the body without those members
   Check: unit
   - setup: a GitHub workspace `demo` (remote `https://github.com/acme/widgets.git`, credential kind `pat`, `forge_api_url` pointing at the test forge) with the caller as its owner
   - setup: a test forge (`httptest` TLS server) that records every request it receives and answers as GitHub or GitLab would
   - setup: an event recorder in place of the event log
   ```
   in internal/forge/write_test.go, a table of body pairs (plain, decorated): POST issues {title:'t'} vs {title:'t', body:null, labels:null, assignees:null, extra:1}; POST pulls {title,head,base} vs the same with body:null, draft:null, extra:{}; POST labels {name:'n'} vs {name:'n', color:null, description:null, x:1}; PATCH issues/7 {title:'t'} vs {title:'t', body:null, state:null, labels:null}: send each, assert both answers have the same status and that the two recorded forge request bodies are equal
   ```
1. [REQ-2.4] IF a measured text (the `body` of an issue create or update, of a comment or of a pull request, or the `comment` of a close) has more Unicode code points than the forge's limit: 65,536 on GitHub, 1,000,000 on GitLab, THEN THE parleyd SHALL refuse the request before anything is sent
   → HTTP 413 with `error_type` `payload_too_large` and a `message` that contains the field's name, the text's length in characters and the limit; the forge receives no request and no event is recorded; a text of exactly the limit is accepted and sent
   Check: unit
   - setup: a GitHub workspace `demo` (remote `https://github.com/acme/widgets.git`, credential kind `pat`, `forge_api_url` pointing at the test forge) with the caller as its owner
   - setup: a GitLab workspace `gl` (remote `https://gitlab.com/group/sub/widgets.git`, credential kind `pat`, `forge_api_url` pointing at the test forge) with the caller as its owner
   - setup: a test forge (`httptest` TLS server) that records every request it receives and answers as GitHub or GitLab would
   - setup: an event recorder in place of the event log
   ```
   in internal/forge/write_test.go, a table over the measured fields {POST issues body, PATCH issues/7 body, POST issues/7/comments body, POST pulls/7/comments body, POST pulls body, POST issues/7/close comment} x {GitHub with 65,536 ASCII characters -> success, GitHub with 65,537 -> 413, GitHub with 65,536 two-byte characters -> success, GitLab with 65,537 -> success}, plus GitLab POST issues body with 1,000,000 ASCII characters -> success and 1,000,001 -> 413: for the 413 rows assert error_type == 'payload_too_large', message contains the field name, the length ('65537' or '1000001') and the limit ('65536' or '1000000'), forge.requests == 0 and events.count == 0; for the success rows assert a 2xx status and that the forge received the text unchanged
   ```

### REQ-3: Create and update an issue

**Rationale:** An agent files and maintains issues without a forge credential (FRG-US-02).

#### Criteria

1. [REQ-3.1] WHEN a caller with write access submits POST /api/v1/workspaces/:slug/issues with a non-blank `title` and optional `body`, `labels` and `assignees`, THE parleyd SHALL create the issue on the forge with the fields that are set and answer with the issue the forge returns
   → HTTP 201 with the issue (`number`, `title`, `body`, `state`, `url`, `author`, `labels`, `created_at`, `updated_at`, `closed_at`, `is_pr`); the forge received one create request carrying the stored token
   Check: unit

   - setup: a GitLab workspace `gl` (remote `https://gitlab.com/group/sub/widgets.git`, credential kind `pat`, `forge_api_url` pointing at the test forge) with the caller as its owner
   - setup: a test forge (`httptest` TLS server) that records every request it receives and answers as GitHub or GitLab would
   - setup: an event recorder in place of the event log
   ```

### REQ-4: Close an issue

**Rationale:** Closing with a reason is one call, and a failure half way leaves a record of what was already posted.

#### Criteria

1. [REQ-4.1] WHEN a caller with write access submits POST /api/v1/workspaces/:slug/issues/:number/close with no body, an empty body, `{}`, `{"comment": null}` or a blank `comment`, THE parleyd SHALL close the issue on the forge without posting a comment, also when the issue is already closed, and answer with the issue
   → HTTP 200 with the issue, whose `state` is `closed`; the forge received exactly one request, the close
   Check: unit
   - setup: a GitHub workspace `demo` (remote `https://github.com/acme/widgets.git`, credential kind `pat`, `forge_api_url` pointing at the test forge) with the caller as its owner
   - setup: a GitLab workspace `gl` (remote `https://gitlab.com/group/sub/widgets.git`, credential kind `pat`, `forge_api_url` pointing at the test forge) with the caller as its owner
   - setup: a test forge (`httptest` TLS server) that records every request it receives and answers as GitHub or GitLab would
   - setup: an event recorder in place of the event log
   ```
   in internal/forge/issue_write_test.go, a table over {GitHub, GitLab} x the bodies {none, empty, `{}`, `{"comment":null}`, `{"comment":"  "}`} x {issue open, issue already closed}: r = post('/workspaces/<slug>/issues/7/close', body); assert r.status == 200 and r.json.state == 'closed'; assert forge.requests == 1 and it is the close (GitHub PATCH issues/7 {state:'closed'}; GitLab PUT issues/7 {state_event:'close'}); assert events.last has no `comment_url`

1. [REQ-4.2] WHEN a caller with write access submits the close route with a non-blank `comment`, THE parleyd SHALL post the comment on the issue first and, after the forge accepted it, close the issue and answer with the issue

   - setup: a GitLab workspace `gl` (remote `https://gitlab.com/group/sub/widgets.git`, credential kind `pat`, `forge_api_url` pointing at the test forge) with the caller as its owner
   - setup: a test forge (`httptest` TLS server) that records every request it receives and answers as GitHub or GitLab would
   - setup: an event recorder in place of the event log

### REQ-8: Forge failures, disconnects and replays

**Rationale:** A caller can tell a forge failure from its own mistake, can retry a create safely, and cannot leave a write half recorded by going away.

#### Criteria

1. [REQ-8.1] IF a forge call of a write route fails, THEN THE parleyd SHALL answer with the status and `error_type` that package 41's mapping gives the failure, with a message from which the workspace's token and URL userinfo are removed
   → forge 404 -> HTTP 404 `forge_not_found`; forge 401 -> 502 `forge_unauthenticated`; forge 403 that is not a rate limit -> 502 `forge_forbidden`; any other forge 4xx -> 422 `forge_rejected`; forge 5xx or an unreadable answer -> 502 `forge_error`; a rate limit that package 41's retry rule does not clear -> 429 `forge_rate_limited` with a `Retry-After` header in whole seconds when the forge stated a wait; no answer within the deadline -> 504 `forge_timeout`; a failed connection -> 502 `forge_unreachable`; the response contains the stored token nowhere
   Check: unit
   - setup: a GitHub workspace `demo` (remote `https://github.com/acme/widgets.git`, credential kind `pat`, `forge_api_url` pointing at the test forge) with the caller as its owner
   - setup: the test forge is set to the behaviour of the row for every request; the forge client is built with a deadline of 200 ms for the timeout row
   - setup: an event recorder in place of the event log
   - setup: the write routes {POST issues, PATCH issues/7, POST issues/7/close, POST issues/7/comments, POST issues/7/labels, DELETE issues/7/labels/bug, POST labels, POST pulls, POST pulls/7/comments}, each with a valid body
   ```

   ```

### REQ-9: Write events

**Rationale:** Every write that reached the forge is auditable, and the audit record holds no user text and no secret (FRG-US-02).

#### Criteria

1. [REQ-9.1] WHEN a write route sent at least one request to the forge and the write succeeded, THE parleyd SHALL record exactly one hub event before it sends the response, with the caller as actor, the written workspace as `workspace`, and the type, `resource_type`, `resource_id`, `action` and metadata of the route
   → per route: issue create -> `parley.forge.issue.create`, `issue`, the new number, `create`; issue update -> `parley.forge.issue.update`, `issue`, the number, `update`, metadata `fields` (names of the fields sent, sorted); close -> `parley.forge.issue.close`, `issue`, the number, `close`, `comment_url` when a comment was posted; issue comment -> `parley.forge.comment.create`, `comment`, the issue number, `create`; add labels -> `parley.forge.label.add`, `label`, the issue number, `add`, `labels`; remove label -> `parley.forge.label.remove`, `label`, the issue number, `remove`, `label`; ensure label -> `parley.forge.label.create`, `label`, the label name, `create`, `label` and `created`; open pull request -> `parley.forge.pull_request.create`, `pull_request`, the new number, `create`, `head`, `base`, `draft`; pull-request comment -> `parley.forge.pull_request.comment`, `pull_request`, the number, `comment`. Every event has metadata `target` and `ok` true, `number` except on the label ensure, and `url` (the web URL of the issue, pull request or comment) except on the three label events; `resource_id` is a string

### REQ-10: CLI commands for forge writes

**Rationale:** The CLI is how most agents reach the hub; every write route has one command.

#### Criteria

1. [REQ-10.1] WHEN a user runs one of `parley issue create`, `parley issue update`, `parley issue close`, `parley issue comment`, `parley label create`, `parley pr create` and `parley pr comment` with valid arguments, THE parley CLI SHALL send the command's route once with a JSON body holding only the fields whose flags were given and with `target` in the query only when `--target` was given, and print the hub's answer
   → stdout is the hub's answer as one JSON document; exit status 0, for `parley label create` both when the hub answers 200 and when it answers 201; the request is: issue create -> POST /api/v1/workspaces/<slug>/issues {title, body, labels, assignees}; issue update -> PATCH …/issues/<number> {title, body, state, labels, assignees}; issue close -> POST …/issues/<number>/close with no body, or {comment} with `--comment`; issue comment -> POST …/issues/<number>/comments {body}; label create -> POST …/labels {name, color, description}; pr create -> POST …/pulls {title, head, base, body, draft}; pr comment -> POST …/pulls/<number>/comments {body}; no `Idempotency-Key` header is sent

## Execution Paths

### PATH-1: An agent files, labels and comments on an issue from the shell

1. **agent** runs `parley issue create demo --title "Flaky test" --label bug` with a PAT that has `forge:write`
2. **parley CLI** sends POST /api/v1/workspaces/demo/issues with the body {"title": "Flaky test", "labels": ["bug"]}
3. **parleyd** checks the scope, write access, the body, the workspace state, the forge configuration, the text limit and the credential kind
4. **parleyd** sends the create request to the forge's API with the workspace's stored token
5. **forge** creates issue 1 and returns it
6. **parleyd** records `parley.forge.issue.create` with `ok` true and answers 201 with the issue
7. **parley CLI** prints the issue on stdout and exits 0
8. **agent** runs `parley issue label demo 1 triage` and `parley issue comment demo 1 --body-file -` with the text on standard input
9. **parleyd** adds the label and posts the comment on the forge, records `parley.forge.label.add` and `parley.forge.comment.create`, and answers 204 and 201
10. **parley CLI** prints the `labeled` confirmation and the comment's `url`, and exits 0 each time

**Smoke check — real components (must not be mocked):** parley CLI commands `issue create`, `issue label` and `issue comment`, parleyd HTTP server with authentication, the scope check and the workspace access rule, forge configuration and forge client of package 41, write handlers, transactional store and secrets store, event log

**Setup:**

- a hub started in-process on 127.0.0.1:0 with a secrets key and a forge transport that trusts the test forge
- a test forge (`httptest` TLS server) that plays GitHub's REST API for one repository and requires the token
- a test origin whose URL path is `/acme/widgets.git`, and the workspace `demo` created through POST /workspaces with `git_pat` and waited for until `ready`
- the workspace setting `forge_api_url` set to the test forge's URL followed by `/github`
- a PAT of the workspace's owner with the scope `forge:write`

**End state:**

- the three commands exit 0; the first prints an issue with number 1, the second `{"status":"labeled","number":1,"labels":["triage"]}`, the third an object with a `url`
- the test forge holds issue 1 with the labels `bug` and `triage` and one comment whose text equals standard input
- every request the test forge received carried the stored token
- the event log holds exactly three forge events for `demo`, of the types `parley.forge.issue.create`, `parley.forge.label.add` and `parley.forge.comment.create`, each with `ok` true
- no command output and no event contains the stored token or the comment text

**Pseudocode:**

```
in test/e2e/forge_write_test.go: forge = newGitHubForge(token); hub = startHub(forgeTransport: forge.client); create workspace demo with git_pat = token; waitReady; patch settings forge_api_url = forge.url + '/github'; out1, c1 = runCLI('issue', 'create', 'demo', '--title', 'Flaky test', '--label', 'bug'); out2, c2 = runCLI('issue', 'label', 'demo', '1', 'triage'); out3, c3 = runCLIStdin(text, 'issue', 'comment', 'demo', '1', '--body-file', '-'); assert c1 == c2 == c3 == 0; assert out1.number == 1 and out2 == {status:'labeled', number:1, labels:['triage']} and out3.url != ''; assert forge.issue(1).labels == ['bug','triage'] and forge.comments(1) == [text]; ev = eventsOf('demo', prefix 'parley.forge.'); assert types(ev) == ['parley.forge.issue.create','parley.forge.label.add','parley.forge.comment.create'] and all ok; assert token and text appear in none of out1..3 and no event
```

### PATH-2: An agent retries opening a pull request and gets one pull request

1. **agent** sends POST /api/v1/workspaces/demo/pulls with `title`, `head`, `base` and the header `Idempotency-Key: pr-1`
2. **parleyd** runs the checks, finds no record for the key and sends the create request to the forge with the workspace's stored token
3. **forge** opens pull request 1 and returns it
4. **parleyd** records `parley.forge.pull_request.create` with `head`, `base`, `draft` and `ok` true, stores the answer under the key and answers 201
5. **agent** does not receive the answer and sends the same request with the same key again
6. **parleyd** finds the record and answers 200 with the first answer, without contacting the forge and without recording an event
7. **agent** sends POST /api/v1/workspaces/demo/pulls/1/comments with a `body`
8. **parleyd** posts the comment in the pull request's conversation, records `parley.forge.pull_request.comment` and answers 201 with the comment's `url`

**Smoke check — real components (must not be mocked):** parleyd HTTP server with authentication, the scope check, the workspace access rule and the idempotency records, forge configuration and forge client of package 41, write handlers, transactional store and secrets store, event log

**Setup:**

- a hub started in-process on 127.0.0.1:0 with a secrets key and a forge transport that trusts the test forge
- a test forge (`httptest` TLS server) that plays GitHub's REST API for one repository, holds the branches `main` and `feature`, and counts the requests it receives
- the workspace `demo` created through POST /workspaces with `git_pat`, waited for until `ready`, with `forge_api_url` set to the test forge's URL followed by `/github`
- a PAT of the workspace's owner with the scope `forge:write`

**End state:**

- the first answer is 201 and the second 200, with equal bodies whose `number` is 1
- the test forge holds exactly one pull request, from `feature` to `main`, and received exactly one create request for it
- the test forge holds one comment on pull request 1
- the event log holds exactly one `parley.forge.pull_request.create` event and one `parley.forge.pull_request.comment` event for `demo`, both with `ok` true

**Pseudocode:**

```
in test/e2e/forge_write_test.go: forge = newGitHubForge(token, branches: ['main','feature']); hub = startHub(forgeTransport: forge.client); create workspace demo; waitReady; set forge_api_url; body = {title:'Add feature', head:'feature', base:'main'}; r1 = post('/workspaces/demo/pulls', body, header Idempotency-Key 'pr-1'); r2 = the same again; assert r1.status == 201 and r2.status == 200 and r2.json == r1.json and r1.json.number == 1; assert len(forge.pulls) == 1 and forge.count('POST', '/repos/acme/widgets/pulls') == 1; r3 = post('/workspaces/demo/pulls/1/comments', {body:'ready for review'}); assert r3.status == 201 and r3.json.url != ''; assert forge.comments(1) == ['ready for review']; ev = eventsOf('demo', prefix 'parley.forge.'); assert types(ev) == ['parley.forge.pull_request.create','parley.forge.pull_request.comment'] and all ok
```

# Tasks

## Test Commands

- **all_tests:** `go test ./... -count=1`
- **linter:** `golangci-lint run ./...`
- **spec_tests:** `go test ./internal/forge/... ./internal/cli/... ./test/e2e/... -count=1`

## Dependencies

- `41` — provides forge detection and configuration, the forge client, the result types, the error mapping and the `issue` and `pr` command groups the write routes and commands build on
- `09` — provides the command helper, HTTP client, output and exit codes the nine write commands use
- `52` — provides the event component every write event is recorded through

**Criteria:** REQ-1, REQ-3.1

**Steps:**

- 1.1 Read what package 41 left in internal/forge: the resolution of workspace, target and forge configuration (repository, forge kind, API URL, credential kind, and the parent for a task fork), the forge client, the issue type with its GitHub and GitLab mappings, and the failure mapping. Use those parts under the names they have; do not write a second resolver, client or mapping
- 1.2 Extend the fake forge of package 41, internal/forge/forgetest, for this package's tests instead of writing a second one: add the write endpoints of GitHub and of GitLab for one repository, keep issues, labels, comments and pull requests in memory, record every request (method, escaped path, headers, body) and let a test make it fail, stall or hold a request
- 1.3 Add the behaviours of this task to internal/forge/write_test.go and internal/forge/issue_write_test.go and confirm they fail. Write the tables that run over every write route against a list of write routes in the test file, to which each later task adds its routes
- 1.4 Add one frame every write handler runs through, in internal/forge/write.go, built on the route helper of package 41 (internal/forge/route.go) with the scope `forge:write` and the need write, and on the hook that helper leaves for the archived and credential checks: the route needs the scope `forge:write` and write access (403 insufficient_scope, 403 forbidden, 404 not_found as the platform's check order gives them), then in this order: target; path parameters and the body rules that do not depend on the forge kind; archived workspace (409 workspace_archived) or, through a fork, archived parent (409 parent_archived); forge configuration (422 forge_api_url_invalid, 422 forge_unknown); the checks that depend on the forge kind; credential kind `none` (422 forge_credential_missing); the call
- 1.5 Give each route two validation hooks in the frame, one that runs before the archived check and one that runs after the forge kind is known, so that later tasks place their rules at the right step
- 1.6 For a fork's slug, act on the parent: require write access on the parent (403 forbidden without it), use the parent's repository, credential and settings, including target=upstream. A fork-bound token of a user with that access is accepted
- 1.7 Send the stored credential as package 41's client does for kind `pat` and `basic`; for target=upstream use the upstream repository, API URL and credential, falling back to the origin credential
- 1.8 Refuse before the call without sending anything to the forge and without recording an event; the frame, not each handler, guarantees it

- 1.10 Mount the route where the hub composes its routes (internal/hub), next to package 41's forge routes

### 2. Validate write bodies and measure text before sending (implement)

**Criteria:** REQ-2

**Steps:**

- 2.1 Add the body and limit behaviours to internal/forge/write_test.go as tables keyed by route and confirm they fail for the create-issue route; later tasks add the rows of their routes
- 2.2 Add body decoding helpers to internal/forge/write.go: a JSON object is required unless the route says otherwise; malformed JSON, a non-object, or a missing body where one is required is 400 invalid_request; unknown members are ignored; a member that is `null` counts as absent
- 2.3 Add field rules that every write route uses: a required string is present and not blank (blank is empty or Unicode white space only); a string, boolean or list member of the wrong JSON type is refused; a list of names has at most 100 entries, each a non-blank string. Each violation is 400 invalid_request with a message that contains the field's name
- 2.4 Add the text limit as a check of the step that depends on the forge kind: count Unicode code points, not bytes; more than 65,536 on GitHub or 1,000,000 on GitLab is 413 payload_too_large with a message that contains the field's name, the text's length and the limit; exactly the limit passes
- 2.5 Apply the rules to the create-issue route: `title` required; `body` a string and measured; `labels` and `assignees` lists of names
- 2.6 Keep the order of the frame: decoding and field rules run before the archived check, the text limit after forge configuration and before the credential check, so that an oversized text on a workspace with an unknown forge answers 422 forge_unknown

- 3.1 Add the event, failure and disconnect behaviours to internal/forge/write_test.go as tables keyed by route and confirm they fail for the create-issue route; later tasks add the rows of their routes. Use an event recorder in place of the event log that notes whether the response had been written when it was called
- 3.2 Give the frame an event step: when a write handed at least one request to the forge client (also one whose connection failed or whose deadline passed), record exactly one event through the event component of package 52 (EmitNow, the form without a caller's transaction) before the response is written; when it handed none, record nothing
- 3.3 Fill the event from the route: its type, `resource_type`, `resource_id` (a string; `none` for a failed create of an issue or a pull request), `action`, the caller as actor, the written workspace as `workspace`, and metadata `target`, `ok`, `error_type` when `ok` is false, `number` and `url` when known, plus the route's extra members
- 3.4 For a call through a fork's slug set `workspace` to the parent and metadata `fork` to the fork's slug; write no `fork` member otherwise
- 3.5 Never put a title, a body, a comment text, a label description, a credential or the forge's error message into an event; a failed write contributes its `error_type` only
- 3.6 Answer a failed forge call with the status, `error_type`, message and `Retry-After` of package 41's failure mapping and scrubbing; do not map failures a second time
- 3.7 Run the forge calls and the event step on a context that is not cancelled when the caller disconnects, keeping the 30-second deadline of each forge request, so that a write runs to its end and records its event
- 3.8 When the event cannot be recorded, answer 500 internal instead of the write's own answer and do not undo what the forge did
- 3.9 Wire the create-issue route to the event step: `parley.forge.issue.create`, resource `issue`, the new number, action `create`, `url` the issue's web URL

### 4. Update issues (implement)

**Criteria:** REQ-3.2, REQ-3.3, REQ-3.4, REQ-3.5

**Steps:**

- 4.1 Add the update behaviours to internal/forge/issue_write_test.go, add the route to the tables of internal/forge/write_test.go, and confirm they fail
- 4.2 Add PATCH /api/v1/workspaces/{slug}/issues/{number} on the frame, with package 41's number rule for `{number}`
- 4.3 Decode `title` (not blank when set), `body` (the empty string is a value and clears the body), `state` (`open` or `closed`), `labels` and `assignees` (an empty list is a value and clears the set); refuse a body that sets none of the five with 400 invalid_request, before the archived check
- 4.4 Send only the set fields. GitHub: PATCH /repos/<owner>/<name>/issues/<n> with title, body, state, labels, assignees. GitLab: PUT /projects/<owner%2Fname>/issues/<n> with title, description, state_event (`close` for `closed`, `reopen` for `open`) and labels as one comma-separated string, the empty string for an empty list
- 4.5 On GitLab never send assignees, on create or on update; when `assignees` is the only set field of an update refuse with 400 invalid_request at the step that depends on the forge kind
- 4.6 Answer 200 with the issue as the forge returns it, through package 41's issue mapping
- 4.7 Record `parley.forge.issue.update` with resource `issue`, the number, action `update`, and `fields`: the names of the fields sent to the forge, sorted, which on GitLab never include `assignees`

### 5. Close issues and post comments (implement)

**Criteria:** REQ-4, REQ-5

**Steps:**

- 5.1 Add the close and comment behaviours to internal/forge/issue_write_test.go and internal/forge/pull_write_test.go, add the three routes to the tables of internal/forge/write_test.go, and confirm they fail
- 5.2 Add POST /api/v1/workspaces/{slug}/issues/{number}/comments and POST /api/v1/workspaces/{slug}/pulls/{number}/comments on the frame: `body` required, not blank, measured against the text limit, sent exactly as given
- 5.3 Post an issue comment with GitHub POST /repos/<owner>/<name>/issues/<n>/comments or GitLab POST /projects/<owner%2Fname>/issues/<n>/notes; post a pull-request comment with the same GitHub call on the pull request's number or GitLab POST /projects/<owner%2Fname>/merge_requests/<n>/notes
- 5.4 Answer 201 with exactly `{"url": <web URL of the comment>}`, taking the URL from package 41's comment mapping so that a written comment has the URL its read gives
- 5.5 Record `parley.forge.comment.create` (resource `comment`, the issue number, action `create`) or `parley.forge.pull_request.comment` (resource `pull_request`, the number, action `comment`), each with `url` the comment's web URL
- 5.6 Add POST /api/v1/workspaces/{slug}/issues/{number}/close on the frame: the body may be absent, empty, `{}` or `{"comment": string}`; a `comment` that is not a string is 400 invalid_request; a non-blank comment is measured against the text limit
- 5.7 With a non-blank comment post it first; when that fails answer its failure and send no close; when it succeeds close the issue (GitHub PATCH issues/<n> with state `closed`; GitLab PUT issues/<n> with state_event `close`). Without one send the close alone. Closing a closed issue is a success
- 5.8 Answer 200 with the issue the close returned
- 5.9 Record one `parley.forge.issue.close` per request that reached the forge (resource `issue`, the number, action `close`), with `comment_url` whenever the comment was posted, also when the close then failed, and `url` the issue's web URL on success

### 6. Add, remove and ensure labels (implement)

**Criteria:** REQ-6

**Steps:**

- 6.1 Add the label behaviours to internal/forge/label_write_test.go, add the three routes to the tables of internal/forge/write_test.go, and confirm they fail
- 6.2 Add POST /api/v1/workspaces/{slug}/issues/{number}/labels on the frame: the body is a bare JSON array of 1 to 100 non-blank strings, anything else is 400 invalid_request. Add the names without replacing the issue's labels (GitHub POST issues/<n>/labels with `labels`; GitLab PUT issues/<n> with `add_labels`, comma-separated). Answer 204 with no body; record `parley.forge.label.add` (resource `label`, the issue number, action `add`, metadata `labels`)
- 6.3 Add DELETE /api/v1/workspaces/{slug}/issues/{number}/labels/{name} on the frame: the name is the last path segment decoded once by the router; a blank name is 400 invalid_request
- 6.4 Remove on GitHub with DELETE issues/<n>/labels/<name as one percent-encoded segment>; when the forge answers 404 read the issue: it exists -> 204, it does not -> 404 forge_not_found; any other failure of either call is mapped as usual. Remove on GitLab with PUT issues/<n> and `remove_labels`; its 404 is 404 forge_not_found
- 6.5 Answer 204 whether or not the issue carried the label; record `parley.forge.label.remove` (resource `label`, the issue number, action `remove`, metadata `label`), with `ok` false and `error_type` forge_not_found when the issue does not exist
- 6.6 Add POST /api/v1/workspaces/{slug}/labels on the frame: `name` required; `color` optional, six hex digits in either case with or without a leading `#`, default `ededed`; `description` optional string
- 6.7 Add the label type {name, color, description} to internal/forge/types.go with its GitHub and GitLab mappings (package 41 has none). Look the label up by name (GET labels/<name as one percent-encoded segment> under the repository or project). Found -> answer 200 with it, unchanged, and send nothing else. A 404 -> create it (colour in lower case, without `#` to GitHub, with `#` to GitLab) and answer 201 with the created label. Any other lookup failure is the answer
- 6.8 When the create is refused because the label now exists (GitHub 422, GitLab 409), look it up once more and answer 200 with it; when that lookup does not find it, answer the create's mapped refusal
- 6.9 Record `parley.forge.label.create` in every case that reached the forge: resource `label`, the label name, action `create`, metadata `label` and `created` (true only when this call created it); no `number` and no `url`

### 9. Add the write commands to the CLI (implement)

**Criteria:** REQ-10

**Steps:**

- 9.1 Add the command behaviours to internal/cli/issue_test.go, internal/cli/pr_test.go and the new internal/cli/label_test.go, against a stub hub, and confirm they fail
- 9.2 Declare every command through the command helper of package 09 with its method and path, and use its client, output and usage errors; reuse the `--target` flag and the `<number>` check of package 41's read commands
- 9.3 Add a text-input helper in internal/cli/textinput.go: `--body <text>` gives the text, `--body-file <path>` reads it from the file, `-` reads standard input; the text is passed on byte for byte; both flags together, or a file that cannot be read, is a usage error; a command says whether one of the two is required
- 9.4 Add to the `issue` group: `create <workspace-slug>` (`--title` required, text input, repeatable `--label` and `--assignee`), `update <workspace-slug> <number>` (`--title`, text input, `--state`, repeatable `--label` and `--assignee`; at least one of them), `close <workspace-slug> <number>` (`--comment`), `comment <workspace-slug> <number>` (text input required)
- 9.5 Build each body from the flags that were given only: a flag that was not given adds no member; `--body ""` on update sends `body` as the empty string; `issue close` sends no body without `--comment`
- 9.6 Add `issue label <workspace-slug> <number> <label>...` (one or more labels, sent as a bare JSON array, prints `{status: labeled, number, labels}`) and `issue unlabel <workspace-slug> <number> <label>` (the label as one percent-encoded path segment, prints `{status: unlabeled, number, label}`); `number` is printed as a JSON number
- 9.7 Add the `label` group with `create <workspace-slug> <name>` (`--color`, `--description`) in the new internal/cli/label.go and register the group on the root command; exit 0 for a 200 and for a 201
- 9.8 Add to the `pr` group: `create <workspace-slug>` (`--title`, `--head`, `--base` required, text input, `--draft` sent only when given) and `comment <workspace-slug> <number>` (text input required)
- 9.9 Raise every usage error before any request: a bad `<number>`, a missing required flag, both text flags, an unreadable body file, `issue update` without a field flag, a wrong argument count. Send no `Idempotency-Key` header
